title: Operator safety journey and microcopy playbook
body:
Summary:
This note captures a small playbook for the operator-facing journey when configuring, launching and observing safe rollouts in the Console. Focus is operator microcopy, control affordances, and edge heuristics that reduce accidental regressions during canary/A-B and auto-fallback scenarios. This is intentionally pragmatic — a mix of sketches, short copy candidates, and a prioritized backlog for design + eng.

Goals:
- Make safety-first defaults obvious and hard to bypass.
- Surface diagnostics that help operators decide whether to continue/abort.
- Provide concise microcopy that reduces cognitive load during incidents.
- Enable quick safe rollbacks and automatic fallback behaviors with clear provenance.

Personas in scope:
- Platform-SRE (operators scheduling rollouts across teams)
- Product manager (observes metrics and signs off on promotions)
- Developer-owner (needs fast iteration with safe guardrails)

High-level flow (operator mental model):
1) Create rollout config (choose target population + model variant + strategy).
2) Dry-run preview (show traffic slices, estimated latency/cost delta, safety heuristics).
3) Start rollout (prompt for minimal escalation approvals only when heuristics are violated).
4) Observe (dashboard with canary-specific probes, realtime alerts).
5) Decision point (continue ramp, pause, rollback, or switch to auto-fallback).
6) Post-mortem notes auto-suggested after termination.

Key UX components and copy samples:
1) Create rollout card (left rail)
- Title: "New rollout"
- Short helper: "Deploy model changes with canary, A/B, or staged traffic. Safety checks run by default."
- CTA: "Configure rollout"

2) Dry-run preview modal
- Heading: "Preview: who will be affected"
- Helper: "This preview simulates traffic slices and shows alarms that would trigger at each step."
- Warnings area header: "Potential blockers"
- No blocker copy: "No safety heuristics flagged — ready to start."

3) Start confirmation (when heuristics breached)
- Modal heading: "Safety checks indicate risk"
- Body: "One or more heuristics (latency increase, error spike, quality regression) exceed recommended thresholds. Proceeding will require explicit confirmation and an approval note."
- Primary CTA: "Start rollout with acknowledgement"
- Secondary CTA: "Adjust thresholds"

4) Running view - canary row item
- Row title: "Canary: 1% → 5% in 30m"
- Micro status: "Healthy — 120s avg latency, 0.2% error"
- Quick action buttons: "Pause | Roll forward | Roll back | Open diagnostics"
- Hover tooltip for Pause: "Immediately stop traffic changes and hold current distribution"

5) Auto-fallback label / banner (when triggered)
- Banner short: "Fallback activated — switching to safe variant"
- Banner body: "Traffic is routed to a proven variant while engineers investigate. You can resume or rollback from the rollout detail page."
- CTA: "View fallback reason"

6) Post-rollback microcopy (toast + journal)
- Toast: "Rollback completed — traffic restored to model v3.4. See notes for triggers."
- Auto-entry in timeline: "Auto-fallback triggered by latency heuristic at 11:12 — switched to v3.4"

Diagnostics and lightweight charts to surface in the running page:
- Canary probe timeline: 1/ success rate, 2/ avg latency, 3/ embedding drift score (where applicable), 4/ quality eval pass rate (if available).
- Difference heatmap: visually highlight metrics that changed > threshold.
- Request-level sampler: display 3 anonymized requests that contributed to metric spikes (redact tokens, show prompthash + classification).

Wireframe notes (structure):
- Left column: rollout config + quick actions.
- Main panel top: live health summary + small multiples for metrics.
- Main panel mid: event timeline (actions, heuristics firing, operator notes).
- Right column: quick diagnostics + recent traces (link to SRE traces).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Operator can define a canary or A/B rollout with safety heuristics enabled by default.
- Console shows dry-run preview with at least latency and error heuristics and an estimated cost delta.
- Running rollout exposes quick actions (pause, forward, rollback) and a single-click fallback trigger.
- Auto-fallback behavior appears with a clear banner + timeline entry and an explanation of the trigger.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How opinionated should defaults be for smaller customers vs enterprise? (low-harm defaults probably universal, stricter heuristics opt-in?)
- Should we include automatic blocked deployments for certain severity heuristic breaches, or leave to operator discretion?
- What level of request sampling is acceptable for privacy/PII constraints? (we should default to hashed prompts + no token retention)
- Where to store operator justification notes for audit (console timeline vs external ticket link)?

Prioritized backlog (short):
- P0: Dry-run preview + safety heuristics enforcement + start confirmation modal (small UX + backend gating).
- P1: Running view charts + quick actions + auto-fallback banner + timeline entries.
- P2: Request sampler, anonymized diagnostics, and microcopy localization.
- P3: Post-mortem structured export and automatic suggested incident template.

Microcopy guidelines (shared across Console):
- Use short verbs for actions (Pause, Roll forward, Roll back).
- Avoid technical jargon in banners; prefer "reverted to safe variant" rather than "fallback to previous model checkpoint" for operator clarity.
- When showing a heuristic, show the metric, the threshold, and the observed value (e.g., "Latency 1,250ms (threshold 900ms)").

Small design experiments to validate quickly:
- AB test two CTAs on the start modal: "Start rollout" vs "Start with safety logs" measuring accidental starts and time-to-first-rollback.
- Inline vs modal dry-run preview: which leads to fewer aborted rollouts?
- Microcopy tone test: neutral ("Proceed") vs prescriptive ("Pause and investigate") and effect on operator behavior.

Next steps / owners:
- Product: finalize acceptance criteria + schedule design spike (Maya).
- Design: quick wireframes + copy variants for the modal and banner (Lina).
- Eng: proto backend hooks for dry-run evaluation and timeline entries (Ben).
- SRE: privacy guidance on request sampling (Arjun).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is deliberately terse. Looking for feedback on the action taxonomy (Pause / Roll forward / Roll back / Fallback) and the proposed dry-run surface. Please add comments inline or drop thoughts in the linked Slack thread.

Appendix — example heuristic table (for engineers to consume):
- latency_p95 increase > 30% for 10m — recommend pause
- error_rate increase > 0.5% absolute — recommend rollback
- embedding_cosine_drift > 0.12 — recommend investigate + optional pause
- unexpected_response_rate (NLP safety model) > 0.1% — immediate rollback (configurable)

References and inspiration:
- Internal: rollout safety policy doc (Confluence)
- External: industry postmortems on dark launches and canary failures

End.
